subject: Re: Featured & Encord - Demo
text:
William,

I stopped by the Encord booth at NeurIPS on Friday looking for you - great
to see Encord have a presence in the back corner in San Diego. Hope the
conference went well.

Here's an honest update on our evaluation.

1. We've decided to be an early design partner with Pipelines
<https://buildpipelines.com/>, a new startup founded by an early ex-Mercor
operations employee. Early design partner essentially means that we get to
share our use case with them, have them develop to our needs, and get
discounted pricing for a set time period.

2. Pipelines should be ready for our use by January 1, which aligns well
with our timeline and prospect pipeline.

3. That said, I'm still evaluating potential secondary use of Encord. My
takeaway from our demo and conversations was that Encord is great at
multi-modal evals, whereas Pipelines is not. We hope to win business from a
lab that has multi-modal eval needs in early Q1, and if we do, we'd need
Encord. If we don't win that business, we're likely set with Pipelines
(assuming that their initial release is good enough to stand up to our
needs).

Bottom line: we're trusting Pipelines to deliver, staying nimble, and are
open to a multi-vendor approach to service any work we win from labs.

Not sure if that's the correct approach, but it's the solution we've
arrived at for now. Is that helpful? Anything else I should be considering?
Appreciate the time committed, and the follow up.

Best,
Brett

subject: Re: Chirag <> Roger
text:
Hi Roger, 

Thanks so much for following up. Let us get back to you but the main issue/challenge is ensuring high quality across multiple datasets as the quality varies significantly. We also have the option to custom collect data for the vendor and can ramp this up with our partners depending on your customer's timeline. 

Separately, I also wanted to follow up on part of your other request. We do have off-the-shelf audio data. Details below. Pricing is roughly $2.50 per hour depending on volume. Samples here

Dataset overview

• 

Type of data: Anonymised multi-channel audio recordings of real-world business conversations, primarily 1:1 calls between businesses and their customers or between two businesses, with a smaller share of multi-party conference calls.

• 

Scale: ~10 million hours of audio suitable for model training.

• 

Geography: Global coverage, with most interactions originating from Europe, North America, and Australia.

• 

Topics / use cases: Calls span a broad range of business functions, including:

• 

Training & education, demos, recruitment, interviews, assessments

• 

Marketing, sales, client interactions

• 

Support, inbound/outbound, screening, follow-up

• 

General admin and other operational conversations

• 

Languages: English (majority of volume), Spanish, German, French, Italian, Portuguese, Swedish, Finnish.

• 

Audio format & structure:

• 

Source captured as 3 channels: Left (Speaker 1), Right (Speaker 2), and a merged mix.

• 

Delivered as separate files per channel (L, R, merged), in MP3 format.

• 

Transcripts & timing:

• 

Full transcripts are available (machine generated)

• 

Each conversation has an associated JSON file with timestamps for the dialogue; 

• 

Metadata (per call) - subject to PII redaction

• 

Phone numbers (source and target)

• 

Call duration

• 

Call direction (inbound / outbound)

• 

Telco outcome (e.g. successful call)

• 

Internal vs external call flag

• 

Category / description of call
